official_measurement_examples.name: SRN scope
official_measurement_examples.fact: DfT Circular 01/2022 applies to England's trunk motorways and all-purpose trunk roads and does not generally apply to the Major Road Network except where it meets the SRN.

official_measurement_examples.name: National Highways consultation role
official_measurement_examples.fact: National Highways is a statutory consultee where proposals may affect SRN safety, queuing, improvement, construction, maintenance or create access to or from the SRN.

official_measurement_examples.name: Highways refusal test
official_measurement_examples.fact: Current NPPF states development should only be prevented or refused on highways grounds where safety impact is unacceptable or residual cumulative network impacts after mitigation are severe, taking reasonable future scenarios into account.

official_measurement_examples.name: Transport-assessment trigger
official_measurement_examples.fact: Developments generating significant movement require a travel plan and appropriate transport statement or assessment; the assessment evaluates impacts and mitigation rather than granting access rights.

official_measurement_examples.name: Network Model limitation
official_measurement_examples.fact: National Highways' public Network Model represents SRN roads open to traffic and validated against its operational boundary, but network geometry alone does not authorise a new private access or junction.

official_measurement_examples.name: P-AMS HAPMS limitation
official_measurement_examples.fact: The July 2026 P-AMS-derived HAPMS layer can indicate National Highways maintenance responsibility and explicitly warns against misuse or misinterpretation; it is not a planning capacity dataset.

official_measurement_examples.name: Roadworks temporal limitation
official_measurement_examples.fact: The National Highways planned-roadworks dataset published 20 July 2026 covers roughly the next 15 days and says it is not real-time information, so it must not be used as a long-term access constraint.

official_measurement_examples.name: Traffic-statistics limitation
official_measurement_examples.fact: DfT road-traffic data provides observed/statistical traffic information at road and count-point scales and does not by itself demonstrate junction capacity or safe access for a proposed development.

core_rules: SRN mapping is road-network evidence not parcel access permission
proximity to a trunk road does not establish a lawful access point
National Highways statutory-consultee status is not planning permission
a Transport Assessment evaluates impacts but does not grant highway rights
a Travel Plan is a management strategy not road capacity evidence
road traffic counts are not junction capacity calculations
P-AMS or HAPMS maintenance geometry is not development-access authority
short-term planned roadworks are not permanent transport constraints
road-condition statistics are not planning refusal criteria
new SRN connections require policy and safety assessment and must not be presumed
NPPF severe residual impact test requires proposal-specific evidence and mitigation context
local transport plans are strategic plans not site access approvals
network geometry does not determine land ownership or private access rights
transport compliance does not reserve development capacity
no parcel highway-access clearance or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
